subject: history
topic: Why the Industrial Revolution caused a permanent shift in human cognition
angle: Industrialisation is linked to a biological mismatch where nature-adapted human biology faces novel challenges and increased stress in modern environments.
title: The Industrial Biological Mismatch

hooks.text: Is your biology out of sync with your life?
You are a nature-adapted organism in an industrial world.
Your environment is keeping your stress response active.
A concrete wall and the hum of electricity.

reveal.headline: Industrialisation created a biological mismatch for humans.
reveal.body: Your biology is adapted for nature, but you live in an industrial world. This shift may have compromised human fitness.

explain.headline: The stress response is constantly active.
explain.body: Chronic activation of stress systems is more pronounced in industrialised areas. Rapid environmental shifts in the Anthropocene may have affected how your body functions.

matters.headline: Your environment may be taxing your biology.
matters.body: That may be why you feel a constant state of tension. Your body is responding to a modern world it was not built to navigate.

example.headline: The hum of a city street.
example.body: The constant noise of traffic and the glow of streetlights at night. Your body registers these as signals in an environment it does not recognize as home.

question.headline: Is your body trying to survive a world it wasn't built for?

verdict: The sources suggest that industrialisation has created a biological and environmental mismatch for humans, but they do not provide specific evidence that it fundamentally rewired attention spans or neural processing.
caveat: The sources do not contain any data regarding industrial time-keeping or specific changes to human attention spans.
caption:
Industrialisation has created a biological mismatch between human biology and our modern environment.

Research suggests that rapid environmental shifts may have compromised human fitness and led to more pronounced stress responses in industrial areas. However, the evidence does not confirm specific changes to neural processing or attention spans.
